source: NTA official JEE Main 2027 syllabus PDF

mathematics: Sets and representation; union, intersection, complement and algebraic properties; power set; relations and equivalence relations; one-one, into and onto functions; composition of functions.

Complex numbers as ordered pairs and a+ib; Argand plane; algebra, modulus and argument; quadratic equations over real and complex systems; roots and coefficients; nature of roots; forming equations from roots.

Matrices and algebra/types; determinants of order two and three; evaluation; triangle area; adjoint and inverse; consistency and solving simultaneous linear equations in two or three variables using matrices.
Fundamental principle of counting; permutations and combinations; P(n,r), C(n,r); simple applications.
Binomial Theorem and its Simple Applications
Binomial theorem for positive integral index; general term; middle term; simple applications.
Arithmetic and geometric progressions; insertion of arithmetic and geometric means; relation between A.M. and G.M.

Real-valued functions and algebra of functions; polynomial, rational, trigonometric, logarithmic and exponential functions; inverse functions and simple graphs; limits, continuity, differentiability; derivatives including composite and implicit functions; second derivatives; rates of change, monotonicity, maxima and minima.

Antiderivatives; standard algebraic, trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic integrals; substitution, parts and partial fractions; trigonometric identities; fundamental theorem; definite-integral properties and evaluation; areas bounded by simple curves.
Ordinary differential equations; order and degree; separation of variables; homogeneous and first-order linear differential equations.

Cartesian coordinates; distance and section formulae; locus; slope and equations of lines; intersections, angles, concurrence and point-to-line distance; triangle centres; circles; standard conics: parabola, ellipse and hyperbola.
Coordinates in space; distance and section formulae; direction ratios and cosines; angle between lines; equation of a line; skew lines and shortest distance.
Scalars and vectors; vector addition; components in two and three dimensions; scalar and vector products.

Mean, median, mode; dispersion, standard deviation, variance and mean deviation for grouped and ungrouped data; event probability; addition and multiplication theorems; Bayes' theorem; probability distribution of a random variable.
Trigonometric identities and functions; inverse trigonometric functions and their properties.
physics: Systems and SI units; fundamental and derived units; least count; significant figures; measurement errors; dimensions and dimensional analysis.

Frames of reference; straight-line motion; speed and velocity; uniform/non-uniform motion; average and instantaneous velocity; uniformly accelerated motion; graphs; relative velocity; motion in a plane; projectile and uniform circular motion.

Force and inertia; Newton's laws; momentum and impulse; conservation of linear momentum; concurrent-force equilibrium; static, kinetic and rolling friction; uniform circular motion; centripetal force; level and banked roads.

Work by constant and variable forces; kinetic and potential energy; work-energy theorem; power; spring potential energy; conservation of mechanical energy; conservative and non-conservative forces; vertical circles; elastic and inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions.

Centre of mass; torque and angular momentum; conservation of angular momentum; moment of inertia and radius of gyration; standard bodies; parallel and perpendicular axes; rigid-body equilibrium and rotation; comparison with linear motion.
Universal gravitation; variation of g with altitude and depth; Kepler's laws; gravitational potential and potential energy; escape and orbital velocity; satellites, time period and energy.

Elasticity and moduli; fluid pressure and Pascal's law; viscosity, Stokes' law and terminal velocity; streamline/turbulent flow and Bernoulli; surface tension and capillarity; thermal expansion, calorimetry, latent heat and heat transfer.
Thermal equilibrium and temperature; zeroth law; heat, work and internal energy; first law; isothermal and adiabatic processes; second law; reversible and irreversible processes.

Ideal-gas equation; work in compression; kinetic-theory assumptions and pressure; temperature interpretation; RMS speed; degrees of freedom; equipartition; specific heats; mean free path; Avogadro's number.

Periodic motion; SHM and its equation; phase; spring oscillations; SHM energy; simple pendulum; wave motion and speed; progressive waves; superposition; reflection; standing waves in strings and pipes; harmonics and beats.

Charge and Coulomb's law; superposition and continuous charge; electric fields and dipoles; flux and Gauss's law; potential and potential energy; conductors, insulators and dielectrics; capacitors, combinations and stored energy.

Current, drift velocity and mobility; Ohm's law; resistance and I-V characteristics; power; resistivity and conductivity; resistor combinations; temperature dependence; cells and internal resistance; Kirchhoff's laws; Wheatstone and metre bridges.
Magnetic Effects of Current and Magnetism

Biot-Savart and Ampere laws; magnetic force on charges and conductors; parallel currents; torque on loops; moving-coil galvanometer; magnetic dipoles and bar magnets; magnetic materials and temperature effects.

Faraday and Lenz laws; induced emf/current; eddy currents; self and mutual inductance; AC peak and RMS values; reactance and impedance; LCR resonance; power and wattless current; generators and transformers.
Displacement current; electromagnetic-wave characteristics and transverse nature; spectrum and applications.

Reflection and mirrors; refraction; thin lenses and lens maker formula; total internal reflection; magnification and lens combinations; prisms; microscopes and telescopes; Huygens principle; interference and Young's experiment; diffraction; polarization and Brewster's law.
Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
Dual nature of radiation; photoelectric effect and observations; Einstein equation; particle nature of light; matter waves and de Broglie relation.
Alpha scattering; Rutherford and Bohr models; energy levels and hydrogen spectrum; nuclear composition and size; mass defect and mass-energy relation; binding energy; fission and fusion.
Semiconductors and diodes; forward/reverse characteristics; rectifiers; LED, photodiode, solar cell and Zener diode; voltage regulation; logic gates.

Measurement with vernier calipers and screw gauge; pendulum energy dissipation; moments; Young's modulus; surface tension; viscosity; resonance tube; calorimetry; metre bridge and Ohm's law; galvanometer; focal length; prism deviation; refractive index; diode and Zener characteristics; component identification.
chemistry: Matter; Dalton's atomic theory; atoms, molecules, elements and compounds; laws of chemical combination; atomic/molecular masses; mole concept and molar mass; percentage composition; empirical/molecular formulae; stoichiometry.

Electromagnetic radiation and photoelectric effect; hydrogen spectrum and Bohr model; dual nature and de Broglie relation; uncertainty principle; quantum model and orbitals; quantum numbers; orbital shapes; spin; Aufbau, Pauli and Hund rules; electronic configurations.

Ionic and covalent bonds; lattice enthalpy; electronegativity and Fajans' rule; dipole moment; VSEPR; valence bond theory and hybridisation; resonance; molecular orbital theory; bond order, length and energy; metallic and hydrogen bonding.

Systems and surroundings; extensive/intensive properties; state functions and entropy; processes; first law, work, heat and internal energy; enthalpy and heat capacities; Hess's law; enthalpy changes; second law, spontaneity, Gibbs energy and equilibrium constant.

Concentration expressions: molality, molarity, mole fraction and percentages; vapour pressure and Raoult's law; ideal/non-ideal solutions; colligative properties; molecular-mass determination; abnormal molar mass and van't Hoff factor.

Dynamic and physical equilibrium; Henry's law; chemical equilibrium, Kp and Kc; Gibbs energy; Le Chatelier's principle; ionic equilibrium; acids and bases; ionisation, pH, common-ion effect, salt hydrolysis, solubility product and buffers.

Oxidation/reduction and oxidation numbers; balancing redox reactions; electrolytic and metallic conduction; molar conductivity and Kohlrausch's law; galvanic/electrolytic cells; electrode potentials; Nernst equation; cell emf and Gibbs energy; batteries and fuel cells.

Reaction rates and factors; elementary/complex reactions; order and molecularity; rate laws and units; zero- and first-order integrated laws and half-lives; Arrhenius theory; activation energy; collision theory.
Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
Modern periodic law and table; s, p, d and f blocks; periodic trends in atomic/ionic radii, ionisation enthalpy, electron-gain enthalpy, valence, oxidation states and reactivity.
Groups 13 to 18; electronic configurations; general trends in physical and chemical properties across periods and down groups; unique behaviour of first elements.

Transition-element configuration and occurrence; trends in physical properties, ionisation enthalpy, oxidation states, radii, colour, catalysis, magnetism and complex formation; interstitial compounds and alloys; KMnO4 and K2Cr2O7; lanthanoids, contraction and actinoids.
Werner's theory; ligands, coordination number and denticity; chelation; IUPAC nomenclature; isomerism; valence-bond and basic crystal-field theories; colour, magnetism and applications.
Purification and Characterisation of Organic Compounds

Crystallisation, sublimation, distillation, extraction and chromatography; qualitative detection of N, S, P and halogens; basic quantitative analysis; empirical/molecular formulae and numerical analysis.
Some Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry

Carbon tetravalency and hybridisation; functional groups and homologous series; structural and stereoisomerism; nomenclature; bond fission; radicals, carbocations and carbanions; electrophiles and nucleophiles; inductive, electromeric, resonance and hyperconjugation effects; reaction types.

Classification, isomerism, nomenclature, preparation, properties and reactions of alkanes, alkenes, alkynes and aromatic hydrocarbons; conformations; addition and substitution mechanisms; ozonolysis; benzene aromaticity and Friedel-Crafts reactions.
Preparation, properties and reactions; C-X bond; substitution mechanisms; uses and environmental effects of chloroform, iodoform, freons and DDT.

Alcohols, phenols, ethers, aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids; preparation, properties, reactions and uses; dehydration; electrophilic substitution; nucleophilic addition; Grignard reagent; oxidation/reduction; aldol, Cannizzaro and haloform reactions; acidity.
Preparation, properties, reactions and uses of amines; nomenclature, classification, structure, basicity and identification; diazonium salts and synthetic applications.
Carbohydrates and constituent sugars; amino acids, peptide bonds and protein structures; denaturation and enzymes; vitamins; DNA and RNA; hormones.

Detection of extra elements and functional groups; preparation chemistry of specified inorganic and organic compounds; titrimetric principles; qualitative salt analysis; enthalpy experiments; preparation of lyophilic and lyophobic sols; kinetic study of iodide and hydrogen peroxide.
